prompt:
A six-panel comic page in bold marker-pen style, TWO ROWS OF THREE panels. The same bus driver — navy coat, glasses — is in every panel, wearing a plain woolly hat and a plain scarf.

HIS HAT, panel by panel: 1 ORANGE, 2 WHITE, 3 GREEN, 4 PURPLE, 5 BLUE, 6 RED.

HIS SCARF MIRRORS THE HATS FROM THE OTHER END OF THE STRIP: the scarf in panel 1 is the colour of the hat in panel 6, the scarf in panel 2 is the colour of the hat in panel 5, the scarf in panel 3 is the colour of the hat in panel 4, and so on back the other way, so the scarf in panel 6 is the colour of the hat in panel 1. Read the scarves backwards and they spell out the hats read forwards.

In no panel do the hat and the scarf share a colour. Six different places on his route, a different pose and framing each time. No text, no captions, no lettering.
easy_question: This image was supposed to show a comic strip: several separate panels, drawn side by side, with the same person appearing in each panel. Ignoring artistic quality and ignoring whether the story is right, does the image DEPICT that — a strip of separate panels with a recurring figure? A comic page, a storyboard or a picture-book strip all count as yes. Answer NO only if it is blank, a single picture with no panels, or something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.
